scope_note: Current U.S. Coinbase Card documentation identifies Pathward, N.A. as issuer. This relation does not describe the separate UK/EU Paysafe-issued card generation.
Current U.S. Coinbase Card documentation identifies Marqeta as the platform powering the card. This relation is not generalized to the separate UK/EU card generation.
Visa is evidenced for the current U.S. Coinbase Card and for the 2019 UK launch and first six-country European expansion. Issuer and processor structure differs by region.
Legacy Bybit.com EEA/CH card terms identify UAB Onlychain Fintech Limited as programme manager; EEA residents were later directed to the separate Bybit EU Card programme.
Legacy Bybit.com terms identify Harmoniie SAS as issuer for EEA countries; this is not generalized to other Bybit Card regions.
Legacy Bybit Card terms identify Moorwand Ltd as issuer for the United Kingdom; this is not generalized to other Bybit Card regions.
Mastercard support is evidenced across current regional programmes and separately in legacy EEA/CH/UK card terms; issuer structure varies by region.
Current Bybit documentation identifies Visa card variants for these regions; this network relationship is region-scoped.
Ledger identifies the CL Card as provided by Baanx. Region-specific legal entities and narrower operational roles are not generalized into this group-level relation.
Ledger's U.S. expansion statement identifies the U.S. CL Card as a Visa crypto card. This relationship is not generalized to other CL Card regions.

The U.S. agreement identifies Foris, Inc. as program manager; the Canadian product page identifies the card as offered by Foris, Inc. Exact relationship start dates differ or are not established across the reviewed regions.
Visa network support is explicitly evidenced in each reviewed region; issuer structure remains region-specific.

Bybit directed legacy Bybit.com EEA/CH card users to apply for a new and separate Bybit EU Card. The 2025-12-31 date was a recommended transition deadline, not proof of individual migration completion.
Bybit EU identifies the program as a Mastercard debit card. Availability is limited to supported European markets and may vary by country.
Wirex EEA terms identify Transact Payments Malta Limited as issuer; eligibility excludes Cyprus and Liechtenstein.
Wirex EEA terms identify Wirex UAB as Program Manager; card eligibility excludes Cyprus and Liechtenstein.
Wirex EEA card terms define Mastercard as the card scheme; card eligibility excludes Cyprus and Liechtenstein.
Wirex Singapore payment-card terms identify Wirex Pte Ltd as Card Issuer.
Historical Bitpanda card terms identify UAB Finansinės paslaugos „Contis“ as issuer/service provider. Bitpanda states the old card was deactivated on 2025-03-31.
Bitpanda's new card became activatable on 2025-04-01; current terms identify Transact Payments Malta Limited as Card Issuer.
Historical Contis terms describe the prior Bitpanda card as Visa; this relation closes with the old-card deactivation date.
Current Bitpanda terms identify the replacement card as a Visa debit card under TPML's Visa licence.
Current U.S. Uphold Visa Card agreement identifies Cross River Bank as issuer; the agreement date is not treated as an exact relationship start date.
Current U.S. card agreement identifies Uphold HQ Inc. as Program Manager for the Uphold Visa Card.
Current U.S. Uphold card agreement identifies the Essential and Elite cards collectively as the Uphold Visa Card on the Visa network.
Contemporaneous closure reporting reproduces the customer notice naming UAB Finansinės paslaugos „Contis“ as issuer. The historical Binance first-party card page was not retrievable in this review.
The discontinued Binance product was a Visa debit card. Closure evidence is contemporaneous reporting quoting Binance rather than a currently retrievable first-party page.
The BlockFi card agreement names Evolve Bank & Trust as Bank. The program became inactive after Visa's 2022-11-16 termination letter; outstanding obligations continued separately.
The card agreement identifies Deserve as Servicer. Evolve later directed former BlockFi cardholders with outstanding balances to Deserve after the card program became inactive.

The BlockFi Rewards Visa Signature Card operated on Visa. The program is treated as ended for card-use purposes when BlockFi's court filing says the Rewards Visa was no longer active following Visa's 2022-11-16 termination letter.
Coinbase's retrospective identifies Shift as the payment processor through which its initial debit card generation was issued. Exact launch and shutdown days are not asserted.
Coinbase states that its initial debit-card generation let customers spend Coinbase bitcoin balances wherever Visa was accepted.

Paysafe issued the UK Coinbase Card launched on 2019-04-10 and the first six-country European expansion announced on 2019-06-11. The relation is left without a single start date because availability was phased by country.
Cryptopay told customers that UAB PAYRNET provided its EU debit-card service and warned users after the provider lost its EMI licence. The relationship is closed on the regulator's revocation date.
Current Cryptopay card terms dated 2025-03-17 identify DiPocket UAB as issuer. The terms date is evidence of the current generation, not asserted as its exact operational cutover date.
Current Cryptopay terms identify CPS Europe S.A. as card programme manager for the DiPocket-issued programme.
Current Cryptopay terms identify the card as a Visa debit card and DiPocket as a Visa principal member.
TenX identifies Wave Crest Holdings Limited as issuer of the historical card generation. The relationship is closed when TenX reported the WaveCrest-issued cards had stopped working in January 2018.
TenX documentation identifies the WaveCrest-issued product as a Visa prepaid card; the reviewed generation ended when the WaveCrest Visa cards stopped working.
Bitwala's own retrospective identifies the WaveCrest dependency and says Visa's termination of the relationship forced Bitwala to halt its debit-card offering.
Bitwala's retrospective ties the historical card shutdown to Visa's termination of the WaveCrest relationship.

Contemporaneous reporting reproduces BitPay's statement that its European card was issued by Wave Crest Holdings Ltd and was no longer available after the January 2018 shutdown. The currently reviewed U.S. BitPay Card is a separate program record.
The historical European BitPay product was a Visa debit card; BitPay explicitly distinguished it from unaffected U.S. card users in the closure statement reproduced by contemporaneous reporting.
WhiteBIT identifies Wallester AS as the issuer and provider of the Nova Visa debit card. The reviewed documentation does not establish a single global relationship start date.
WhiteBIT documents Nova as a Visa debit card and identifies Wallester as a Visa Principal Member.
Bitget's APAC launch material identifies DCS Card Centre Pte. Ltd. as the issuing collaborator for the Bitget Card generation launched on 2026-04-02.
Bitget's APAC launch and cardholder terms identify the reviewed generation as a Visa card program.
Xapo support identifies Xapo Bank as the issuing bank authorising Xapo Card transactions. The reviewed material does not establish an exact relationship start date.
Xapo support documents Visa network variants of the Xapo Card, including additional restrictions for European Visa cards; this relation does not imply every Xapo Card is Visa.
Xapo support documents Mastercard network variants of the Xapo Card; this relation does not imply every Xapo Card is Mastercard.
RedotPay identifies StraitsX as BIN sponsor for its Singapore Visa card programme. No issuer role is inferred and this relation is not generalized to the separate Hong Kong programme.
Current RedotPay terms explicitly identify both the Hong Kong and Singapore card programmes as Visa programmes; regional issuer/BIN-sponsor structures are not generalized.
SafePal identifies Fiat24 as the provider powering the in-app Fiat Gateway and linked card service. The provider role is not narrowed beyond the evidence.

Current SafePal material documents Mastercard debit-card support. SafePal's 2024 launch described a Visa card, but the exact operational network cutover date is not established, so no start date is invented here.
Ready's privacy/security FAQ identifies Kulipa as the regulated card issuer. The reviewed source does not establish an exact relationship start date.
Ready identifies the Ready Card as a debit card usable wherever Mastercard is accepted.
KuCoin's KuCard terms identify Wallester AS as issuer of the Visa debit card. No exact issuer-relationship start date is asserted from the reviewed terms.
KuCard terms identify UAB EURLITA as the Partner providing KuCard services on Wallester's behalf. This relation does not assign an issuer role.
KuCard is explicitly documented as a Visa debit card for the reviewed EEA program.
Oobit's current card terms explicitly define ThirdNational as issuer for the reviewed card program. The registry does not expand the issuer name beyond the reviewed disclosure.
Current Oobit card terms and the U.S. launch material identify Visa acceptance for the reviewed wallet-native card program.
Bit2Me's current card terms identify PECUNIA CARDS EDE, S.L.U. / Pecunpay as issuer of the Bit2Me card and payment account.
Bit2Me's card terms also identify Pecunpay as manager of the card and payment account, separately from the Mastercard network role.
Bit2Me launched the product as a Mastercard debit card and current legal terms continue to identify the reviewed card as Mastercard.

Plasma's current product disclosure states that the Plasma One Card is issued by Rain, a Visa Principal Member. Bridge-powered account services vary by region and are not collapsed into this issuer relation.
Plasma identifies Plasma One as a Visa card issued by Rain under a Visa licence and usable wherever Visa is accepted in supported markets.

Jupiter states that Rain is one of two card issuers assigned automatically according to the user's country of residence. This relation does not imply simultaneous issuance with DCS for one cardholder.

Jupiter states that DCS is one of two card issuers assigned automatically according to the user's country of residence. This relation does not imply simultaneous issuance with Rain for one cardholder.
Jupiter documents the Jupiter Card as a Visa debit card; issuer assignment between Rain and DCS depends on country of residence.
Slash's launch announcement states that its Global Cards are issued by partner Rain. This record is separate from the regular Slash Platinum charge card issued by Column N.A.
Slash documents the Global Card as a Visa card funded from the Global USD stablecoin balance through Rain.
MEXC's launch announcement identifies MEXC Global Card as a Visa card. The precise regulated issuing entity remains unresolved and no issuer relation is inferred.
Current Bleap EEA cardholder terms define Unlimit EU Ltd as the Issuer that issues the Card and e-money. The terms do not establish an exact operational relationship start date.
Bleap's EEA cardholder terms define the product as a Mastercard debit card; the earlier partnership announcement also identifies Mastercard.
Gate US identifies the Gate Card as a prepaid Visa card issued by Lead Bank, Member FDIC, under a Visa licence.
Gate US launch and product disclosures identify Visa as the network for the U.S.-scoped Gate Card.
Gate US identifies Bridge as program manager responsible for managing and operating the card on behalf of Lead Bank.
Gate US's launch announcement states that Bridge participates in the underlying stablecoin infrastructure and settlement capabilities. This does not assign Bridge an issuer role.

THORWallet's current first-party material identifies Mastercard acceptance for the Basic/Premium card generation. No issuer or program-manager relation is inferred because current first-party/legal evidence reviewed here does not establish that role.
LBank's 2026 relaunch announcement identifies Visa merchant acceptance for the current LBank Card. The precise regulated issuer remains unresolved.
MetaMask's U.S. general-availability announcement identifies Cross River Bank as issuer for the U.S. MetaMask Card.
MetaMask's U.S. launch announcement describes the card as powered by Baanx, noting the subsequent Monavate identity. This relation is scoped to the evidenced U.S. launch stack.
MetaMask's U.S. launch announcement identifies Monavate in the Baanx/Monavate card-infrastructure context. No issuer role is assigned to Monavate for this MetaMask relation.
Mastercard's launch announcement identifies the Brazil-scoped Binance Card as a Mastercard product. The regulated issuer and processor remain unresolved in the reviewed first-party source.
Current 1inch terms identify the 1inch CL Card as a prepaid Mastercard issued by Monavate Limited.
1inch launch and current terms identify Mastercard as the card network.
1inch identifies Crypto Life as powering the 1inch Card.
Current 1inch card documentation describes the product as developed in partnership with Baanx; no issuer role is assigned to Baanx here.

Kraken identifies Monavate Limited as UK issuer and UAB Monavate as EEA issuer. The existing Monavate provider record is reused while the jurisdiction-specific legal-entity wording is preserved in evidence and scope.
Kraken's launch and product pages identify Kraken Card as Mastercard debit card.
Coinbase's current Coinbase One Card disclosure identifies First Electronic Bank as issuer.
Coinbase states the Coinbase One Card is offered through Coinbase, Inc. and Cardless, Inc. No regulated issuer role is assigned to Cardless.
Coinbase identifies American Express as the network for the Coinbase One Card.
Mercuryo's Ledger-compatible Spend launch explicitly identifies Quicko Sp. z o.o. as issuer for the virtual card offered to EEA users at that launch.
Mercuryo describes Spend as a Mastercard crypto debit card. The 2025 Ledger integration and current support material both identify Mastercard acceptance.

Current Kolo Terms state that Card Services are provided in collaboration with Signify Holdings Inc. and link that provider to Rain Cards. This records the evidenced card-service relationship without assigning Rain an issuer role.
Kolo's first-party card material describes Kolo Card as Mastercard-backed for its current EEA/Ukraine availability. No issuer is inferred from network branding.
Avalanche Card's reviewed U.S. Cardholder Agreement identifies Third National / Third National, Inc. as issuer. This relation is not generalized to jurisdictions governed by other issuing partners.
Avalanche Card is offered and powered by Rain Liquidity; the U.S. agreement also identifies Rain Liquidity as service partner. No broader issuer role is assigned to Rain for the U.S. program.
Current Avalanche Card materials and the U.S. card agreement identify Visa as the payment network.
Phantom's U.S. open-access announcement identifies Lead Bank as issuer of the prepaid Visa debit card.
Phantom identifies Bridge Ventures LLC as Program Manager responsible for managing and operating the card on behalf of Lead Bank.
Phantom identifies the product as a prepaid Visa debit card usable wherever Visa is accepted.
Bitget Wallet documents Mastercard variants of the card, with network and issuing partner varying by region.
Bitget Wallet's Mainland China card help documentation identifies a partnership with Fiat24. This regional relation is not generalized to other Bitget Wallet Card markets.
Bitget Wallet documents Visa variants of the card, with network and issuing partner varying by region.
Current Ripio Card terms identify Digipayments S.A.U. as one of two co-issuers. No earlier start date is inferred from the current agreement.
Current Ripio Card terms identify Pomelo Fintech Services S.A.S. as one of two co-issuers.
Pomelo describes its payment-processing infrastructure as powering the Argentina Ripio Card launch; the current Ripio terms also retain Pomelo in the card stack.
Current Ripio terms identify Visa acceptance in Argentina; the 2023 Argentina launch generation is also documented as Visa.
Current Buenbit terms explicitly identify BKR ARGENTINA S.A. as the issuer of the prepaid Mastercard.
Mastercard's Buenbit relaunch statement identifies Pomelo as the strategic infrastructure partner for the 2022 generation. No current issuer role is assigned to Pomelo for Buenbit.
Current Buenbit terms and the 2022 relaunch statement identify Mastercard as the network.
belo and Mastercard identify the Argentina prepaid card as Mastercard. No issuer relation is inferred from weaker third-party material.

Digifin's current prepaid-card terms identify Digifin S.A. as the company issuing and providing the Tarjeta Prepaga Lemon. The 2021 historical launch date is recorded separately as a program event rather than asserted as the issuer-relation start date.
Lemon's launch-era and current documentation identify the Argentina prepaid Lemon Card as Visa.
Digifin's credit-card terms explicitly define the Lemon crypto-collateralized credit card as a physical credit card issued by Digifin S.A.
Digifin terms and Lemon's launch statement identify Visa as the network for the Bitcoin-backed credit-card program.
Current Takenos TakeCard terms require acceptance of Rain provider terms. This records the evidenced provider relationship without assigning Rain an issuer role.
Current Takenos help and product materials identify TakeCard as an international prepaid Visa card issued in the United States.
